title: Customers reach a first useful search result quickly
acceptanceCriteria: A documented onboarding path registers one content source through the sources API and returns a ranked result from the search API, and an automated end-to-end test exercises that path.
The service records the time from source connection to first search result per customer, and the repository documents the target and the owner who reviews misses.

title: Search improves measurable customer outcomes
acceptanceCriteria: Versioned outcome definitions measure search success rate, zero-result queries, document freshness, and time saved by customer cohort.
Ranking confidence and incomplete source coverage remain visible beside every result-quality metric in customer and executive reports.

title: Search ranking remains explainable
acceptanceCriteria: Each ranked result traces to the versioned index build, the ranking model version, the source document, and the features that produced its score.
Relevance feedback, manual overrides, and their reasons are recorded and feed an auditable ranking improvement loop.

title: Content sources connect through stable contracts
acceptanceCriteria: Versioned APIs and connector contracts cover source registration, document ingestion, search, and result export, and contract tests block breaking changes.
Signed webhooks use bounded retries, replay protection, dead-letter recovery, and delivery reconciliation.

title: Every customer's documents and workload stay isolated
acceptanceCriteria: Tenant scope is enforced across document storage, search indexes, caches, queues, exports, and support access.
Automated negative tests reject cross-tenant reads, changes, enumeration, and noisy-neighbor failures.

title: Changes ship with repeatable confidence
acceptanceCriteria: Automated unit, integration, contract, migration, and end-to-end tests run in CI gates and block incompatible releases.
Dependency vulnerability, update, and license policies produce reviewable release evidence.

title: Service health is observable and actionable
acceptanceCriteria: Structured logs, metrics, traces, synthetic checks, SLOs, and alerts cover the ingestion, search, and webhook delivery paths.
Tested backup and restore, rollback, and incident procedures meet committed recovery targets.

title: Growth preserves predictable performance and cost
acceptanceCriteria: Load tests enforce latency, throughput, and cost targets across representative document-corpus sizes and ingestion bursts.
A clean-machine developer bootstrap and documented architecture let engineers reproduce and diagnose the system.

title: AI-assisted engineering stays verified, bounded, and traceable
acceptanceCriteria: A version-controlled agent contract (for example AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md) states the repository's invariants, the verification recipe, and the checks an agent must run before proposing a change.

A repository-local verification harness launches the service, checks its health, drives at least one user-facing feature, captures evidence, and cleans up, so a change is proven to work at runtime rather than only compiling.
Agent-authored and human-authored changes pass the same enforced CI gates plus that runtime verification step before merge, and agent commits are attributed and signed off.
Design decisions are recorded in version control (for example a decision log) and a module map documents where behavior lives, so agents and reviewers can trace why and where without archaeology.
Agent tool access is least-privilege in code: read-only by default, with write, network, and execution scopes explicit and auditable.
